# Office SDK

Office SDK is an embedded web document surface for products that need Office file workflows to stay beside the surrounding record, permissions, and business process.

## Core pages

- [Home](https://officesdk.com/): product position, editor story, format families, and FAQ.
- [Product](https://officesdk.com/product): embedded preview, editing, collaboration, import, export, and ownership boundaries.
- [Core editor story](https://officesdk.com/product/core-editors): one illustrative launch across notes and Markdown, Word, Excel, and PowerPoint using privacy-redacted product screenshots of the imported templates.
- [Formats](https://officesdk.com/formats): operation-specific format coverage for preview, import, edit, and export.
- [Solutions](https://officesdk.com/solutions): content platforms, review and approval, education and research, and business systems.
- [Deployment](https://officesdk.com/deployment): proof of concept, browser delivery, deployment baseline, and operating ownership.
- [Journal](https://officesdk.com/blog): practical articles on integration, security, migration, AI documents, and operations.
- [Docs](https://officesdk.com/docs): documentation reading path — quickstart, frontend embed, backend callbacks, and deployment guides.
- [Demo](https://officesdk.com/demo): self-guided editor story and guided session options for evaluating the surfaces.
- [Pricing](https://officesdk.com/pricing): self-hosted licensing model sized by editors, environments, and workflow scope.
- [Contact](https://officesdk.com/contact): workflow, file, and deployment questions for the Office SDK team.

## Verified scope

- The first editable Office families to evaluate are Word, Excel, and PowerPoint.
- Broader preview candidates listed on the site include PDF, OFD, images, video, audio, text, and Markdown.
- The host product owns users, file storage, permission decisions, and business records.
- A focused single-server proof of concept comes before production deployment planning.
- Preview, import, edit, review, and export are separate acceptance decisions.

## Editorial use

Use the Journal to frame a document task, identify the system boundary, test the file and version path, and retain observed evidence with the decision. Article references remain linked to their original sources.
